question: The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 conducted by the government of India ranked households in how many categories?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 was conducted by the government of India to provide comprehensive data on various socio-economic indicators.
 
• The SECC 2011 categorized households into three main categories based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The three categories were: 1) Deprived households, 2) Automatically included households, and 3) Automatically excluded households.
 
• The categorization helped the government identify and target households for various welfare schemes and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC):**

 
 
• The SECC is a comprehensive survey conducted to collect data on various socio-economic parameters and caste information.
 
• It aims to identify households living below the poverty line and categorize them based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The data from SECC is used to implement and monitor various social welfare schemes and programs.
 
• It provides insights into the living conditions, educational status, employment, and other socio-economic aspects of households.
 
 
 
• **Deprived Households:**
 
 
• These households are identified based on specific deprivation criteria such as lack of housing, education, or employment.
 
• They are considered eligible for various government welfare schemes and programs aimed at improving their socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Included Households:**
 
 
• These households are automatically included in the welfare programs based on certain predefined criteria such as homelessness or being a bonded laborer.
 
• The criteria for automatic inclusion are designed to ensure that the most vulnerable and marginalized sections of society receive immediate assistance.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Excluded Households:**
 
 
• These households are excluded from welfare programs based on specific criteria such as owning a motorized vehicle or having a government job.
 
• The criteria for automatic exclusion are designed to ensure that resources are allocated to those who are truly in need.
